correctness.rationale: The fixed-iid one-step decrement is exactly the smallest eigenvalue of B^T diag(p) B; congruence gives a minimum-trace diagonal PSD majorant of C=(BB^T)^-1. In the weak branch the slack has a displayed positive sum-of-squares decomposition, matching the dual all-ones Gram matrix. In the strong branch it factors into a rank-one PSD term plus a complete-graph Laplacian, matching the dual two-rank-one Gram X. These prove equality for all real t>0 and all integer n>=5, without symmetry assumptions on competitors. Complementary slackness forces every optimum diagonal uniquely; rank calculations yield the exact boundary. An implicit-function argument independently establishes feasibility for sufficiently small w. The delivered standard-library verifier passed 47,263 checks across 124 rational certificate cases and 28 normalized actual systems; finite checks do not prove infinite statements.

value.rationale: The sign and scale of one antagonistic coupling in an otherwise homogeneous inverse-Gram clique is a natural correlated-equation robustness question. The new exact sampling law covers an infinite dimension family and has an unexpected sharp transition at t=(n-2)/2, separating signed-row-sum and rational regimes with a nullity jump. Dense redundancy raises the necessary antagonism with dimension in contrast to sparse cycles, so this is structural knowledge beyond an arbitrary narrow instance. It replaces a semidefinite program with an implementable unique probability vector and exact worst-case one-step contraction; no unsubstantiated multistep advantage is claimed.
